headline: Salt Lake looks like salt, snow and sandstone, drawn on a grid and printed by hand.
summary: Salt Lake's visual culture sits between an orderly city grid and an outdoor-art tradition. The working scene is artist-run and DIY, from Central 9th, Sugar House and downtown to Craft Lake City and the Utah Arts Festival. Dress the gray City Edition in real Utah materials and local makers, not mountain clip art. Keep LDS sacred imagery off it, and never flatten Pacific Islander culture into decoration.

insights.title: The grid is the graphic language
insights.detail: Salt Lake addresses are coordinates: 900 South and 900 East, shortened locally to 9th and 9th, or 2100 South, or "the West Side." Residents use these numbers as neighborhood identity. They sit beside the beehive iconography and mid-century signage that give the city its orderly look.
insights.implication: Put numeric grid coordinates in a clean sans on tees, jock tags and hangtags. They are more ownable than another mountain silhouette, and nobody else can swap them in.

insights.title: Salt, snow and shale beat generic mountain
insights.detail: The current Jazz City Edition is a vertical gray gradient with baby blue trim. It maps onto Wasatch granite, inversion haze and winter dawn, and onto the pale texture of the Bonneville Salt Flats and the Great Salt Lake shoreline.
insights.implication: Build graphics from real surfaces: crusted salt, shale, snow-pack. Then the gray palette reads as place, not a default colorway.

insights.title: Land art is the city's signature art world
insights.detail: Utah is a land-art pilgrimage. Robert Smithson built Spiral Jetty at Rozel Point on the Great Salt Lake in 1970, and Nancy Holt set her Sun Tunnels in the Great Basin desert in 1976. The lake's low water and pink microbial color shifts are a live civic concern.
insights.implication: A spiral or shoreline-contour motif can anchor a collection. Credit and license anything derived from Smithson's work (estate and Holt-Smithson Foundation), and consider a Great Salt Lake conservation tie-in.

insights.title: Artist-run DIY and print culture drives the scene
insights.detail: Monthly Gallery Stroll, Craft Lake City's DIY Fest, screen-print and poster shops, and the downtown and Central 9th studio clusters feed the scene. It runs on local illustrators and muralists more than on a gallery market.
insights.implication: Commission two or three local artists through a paid, credited program for a limited graphic drop. Don't source a single "Utah" look in Portland.

insights.title: Two Jazz eras, both worth drawing
insights.detail: The franchise carries the 1979-96 musical-note look and the 1996-2004 purple, teal and copper mountain era. Its New Orleans legacy is heritage to Utah fans, not baggage.
insights.implication: Run purple-and-mountain throwbacks beside the gray City Edition as a heritage lane. Check licensing on legacy marks with the team and NBA.

insights.title: West Side culture is visually underserved
insights.detail: Utah has one of the largest per-capita Pacific Islander populations in the US, concentrated in West Valley City, Kearns, Rose Park and Glendale. Glendale and Rose Park also have a visible Latino presence. Community anchors include Centro Civico Mexicano and the Mestizo Institute of Culture and Arts, both to be confirmed as active. The Jazz come off a 22-60 season, but a young core of Darryn Peterson, Ace Bailey, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. brings fresh fans from these communities.
insights.implication: Co-create with community designers, tattoo artists and church or school groups. Never lift tatau, tapa or other ceremonial patterns without family or community permission and payment.

places.name: Utah Museum of Contemporary Art (UMOCA)
places.why: The city's main contemporary art institution and a credible partner for local artist commissions.

places.name: Utah Museum of Fine Arts (UMFA)
places.why: The state's major art museum, on the U campus. Useful for archive and design-history access.

places.name: Poor Yorick Studio
places.why: Independent print studio tied to the local printmaking scene. Operating status and location are unconfirmed.

places.name: Central 9th and 9th and 9th
places.neighborhood: 900 South, west side of downtown and 900 East
places.why: Two distinct 900 South hubs. Central 9th (around 200 West) is a mural and studio cluster. 9th and 9th (around 900 East) has shops and cafes. Both carry the numbered-grid vernacular.

places.name: Sugar House
places.why: Home to the Sugar House Monument, small shops and murals. A walkable core that draws fans.

places.name: Utah State Fairpark
places.why: Hosts Craft Lake City's DIY Fest, the busiest local-maker marketplace of the year.

places.name: Library Square
places.why: Home of the Utah Arts Festival each June. Moshe Safdie's architecture frames the city's modern look.

places.name: Spiral Jetty (Rozel Point)
places.neighborhood: Great Salt Lake north shore, Box Elder County
places.why: The state's best-known artwork and an anchor for salt-and-spiral imagery.

places.name: Delta Center
places.why: The home arena. The surrounding downtown blocks and signage are the natural canvas for a launch.

people.name: Trent Call
people.why: A widely recognized Utah artist whose large figurative and mural work makes him a credible collaborator for a limited graphic.

people.name: Sri Whipple
people.why: Known locally for bright, community-minded murals. A plausible partner for a street-level graphic.

people.name: Ben Wiemeyer
people.why: Salt Lake artist known for large murals and graphic-forward illustration.

people.name: Robert Smithson
people.why: His work defines Utah in art history. Any reference needs estate engagement, not casual borrowing.

people.name: Craft Lake City
people.role: Local nonprofit and DIY Fest organizer
people.why: Runs the main annual maker marketplace and can introduce vetted local designers and screen printers.

people.name: Salt Lake Arts Council
people.why: Runs Living Traditions and public-art programs. A route to community artists, including Pacific Islander and Latino makers.

moments.name: Gallery Stroll
moments.why: The recurring downtown opening night for galleries. An easy pop-up and artist-meet night.

moments.name: Living Traditions Festival
moments.why: A free festival of the area's ethnic and folk arts. The place for Pacific Islander, Latino and other community crafts.

moments.name: Utah Arts Festival
moments.why: Library Square festival with visual artists. A likely launch moment for a collab with a local artist.

moments.name: Craft Lake City DIY Fest
moments.why: Peak local-maker visibility, and the best place to find future collaborators.

moments.name: Kimball Arts Festival
moments.why: Park City's juried arts festival, drawing the affluent mountain-town crowd.

moments.name: Jazz vs. Nuggets, NBA Cup group opener
moments.why: The Jazz's first Cup night at home. An obvious early-season drop or window launch.

vocabulary.meaning: Local shorthand for the 900 South and 900 East intersection and its shop-and-cafe neighborhood. Not to be confused with Central 9th near 200 West.
The numbered street system radiating from Temple Square. Locals use it constantly for directions and identity.
Rose Park, Glendale and neighboring communities west of I-15, with strong Pacific Islander and Latino roots.
The winter haze that traps cold air in the valley. Everyone sees it and shares it.
Utah's state emblem, for industry. It shows up on signs, highways and the state flag.
The state ski-tourism slogan on license plates. It is a state-tourism phrase, so treat it as a reference, not a free slogan.
The mountain range behind the city and the dominant skyline shape.

designCues.use: Base of the vertical fade, paired with a cooler top tone for a skyline-at-dawn effect.

designCues.source: The current City Edition accent, matched to the high-desert morning sky
designCues.use: Trim, piping and tonal embroidery. Keep it consistent with the on-court uniform.

designCues.source: The lake's seasonal pink water in the north arm
designCues.use: A small accent for a drop graphic or lining. Keep it from dominating, to protect the Jazz's identity.

designCues.source: Southern Utah canyon country, Arches and Zion
designCues.use: Warm counter-color for outdoor-oriented apparel, used sparingly.

designCues.source: The 1990s purple, teal and copper mountain era and the original note-era palette
designCues.use: Throwback line, with legacy marks licensed through the team and NBA.

designCues.source: The Bonneville Salt Flats and Great Salt Lake shoreline
designCues.use: Tonal print or jacquard on shorts, warm-up shells and bags.

designCues.source: Salt Lake's numbered street addresses such as 900 South and 2100 South
designCues.use: Clean sans numerals as graphics, and on jock tags and sleeve hits.

designCues.source: Spiral Jetty and Great Salt Lake contour maps
designCues.use: Tonal line graphic on a hoodie or tee. License and credit anything drawn from Smithson's work.

productHooks: "Grid" graphic tee and hoodie in the gray gradient with baby blue accents, built on Salt Lake coordinate addresses and printed in a limited run by a local screen shop.

Paid, credited collaboration with one or two Utah muralists or illustrators (for example Trent Call, Sri Whipple or Ben Wiemeyer, pending outreach). Time the numbered release to the Cup opener or Gallery Stroll.
Heritage Purple throwback capsule in the 1990s mountain-era palette, subject to license, as a counterpart to the gray City Edition.
Salt-crust and shale tonal-texture warm-up jacket and bag set, with a donation tied to Great Salt Lake conservation.
watchouts: Keep the Salt Lake Temple, temple iconography and other LDS sacred imagery or garment-related references off product.
Pacific Islander designs such as tatau, tapa and Hawaiian or Tongan ceremonial patterns need community partnership, credit and payment. Never lift them.
Spiral Jetty imagery and any Smithson-derived work involve estate rights. Clear the Utah state flag, beehive emblem and tourism slogans too, as government IP.
Legacy Jazz marks (note, purple mountain) belong to the team and NBA. Coordinate all use.
